_metadata.description: RVA23S64 Extension Software Stack Coverage Matrix (supervisor-mode profile additions)
_metadata.udb_source: riscv-unified-db spec/std/isa/profile/RVA23S64.yaml (inherits RVA23U64 + RVB23S64; adds Sha, Ssnpm; chain: RVA20S64 -> RVA22S64 -> RVB23S64 -> RVA23S64)
_metadata.scope_note: This matrix lists only the S-mode/H-mode/M-mode-privileged extensions that RVA23S64 adds on top of RVA23U64. All RVA23U64 mandatory and optional extensions remain mandatory/optional here too - see the RVA23U64 tab for those. Sub-extensions implicitly required by a mandatory umbrella are omitted (per the U64 editorial policy): Shgatpa, Shtvala, Shvsatpa, Shvstvala, Shvstvecd, Shcounterenw are subsumed under Sha (which requires H + Ssstateen + several Sh* sub-properties); Sha itself is the umbrella name and is represented here via its constituents H + Ssstateen.

layer_definitions.none: No new instructions. Platform property guarantee only - hardware must meet this constraint, but software (kernel, userspace) needs no changes.
layer_definitions.compiler: Has ISA instructions that the compiler can auto-generate when -march enables the extension.
layer_definitions.kernel: Requires kernel changes (typical for S-mode extensions: page table semantics, signal/trap handling, perf, timer, virt).
layer_definitions.userspace: Requires userspace runtime library changes beyond what the compiler provides.
layer_definitions.full_stack: Impacts the entire stack: kernel, compiler, and userspace libraries all need changes.

mandatory.name: S
mandatory.layer_note: Foundational privilege level. Linux runs in S-mode. Trap entry/exit, page table base (satp), interrupt delegation (mideleg/medeleg).

mandatory.name: H
mandatory.description: Hypervisor support: VS/VU virtualization modes, two-stage translation, hypervisor CSRs and instructions
mandatory.layer_note: Mandatory in RVA23S64 via the Sha umbrella. KVM-RISCV depends on H. Kernel: hypervisor state save/restore, two-stage translation (hgatp/G-stage), VS-mode timer/interrupts, hypervisor instructions (hfence.vvma/gvma, hlv/hsv, hinval.*). Userspace: VMM (QEMU, kvmtool) drives /dev/kvm ioctls; no direct H-instruction emission.

mandatory.name: Ssstateen
mandatory.description: sstateen0..3 / hstateen* / mstateen* CSRs gating lower-privilege access to extension state
mandatory.layer_note: Gates U-mode and VU-mode access to other-extension state (Zcmt jvt, Sha CSRs, future extensions). Kernel must save/restore sstateen* across context switch and selectively grant userspace access. Required by Sha. Distros need this plumbed into the ptrace regset.

mandatory.name: Sscofpmf
mandatory.description: scountovf CSR + per-counter privilege filter (M/S/U/VS/VU inhibit) bits in mhpmeventN
mandatory.layer_note: Linux perf subsystem reads scountovf to handle HPM counter overflow interrupts in S-mode (no SBI ecall hop). Per-counter privilege filtering (e.g., kernel-only sampling) drives mhpmevent inhibit bits. Userspace 'perf' tool consumes via perf_event_open syscall.

mandatory.name: Sstc
mandatory.description: stimecmp / vstimecmp CSRs for direct supervisor-mode timer programming
mandatory.layer_note: Replaces sbi_set_timer ECALL with direct stimecmp CSR write. Linux already gates on RISCV_ISA_SSTC and falls back to SBI when unavailable. Significant timer-IRQ latency win and boot-path simplification. VS-mode mirror vstimecmp benefits KVM-RISCV guests.

mandatory.name: Ssnpm
mandatory.description: Pointer masking CSR control at S-mode (senvcfg.PMM, henvcfg.PMM for VS)
mandatory.layer_note: Kernel side of the U-mode pointer-masking feature (the Supm announcement in RVA23U64). Kernel configures senvcfg.PMM to set PMLEN, handles the prctl(PR_SET_TAGGED_ADDR_CTRL) opt-in, preserves PMLEN across context switch, and exposes it to ptrace.

mandatory.name: Svinval
mandatory.layer_note: Decouples TLB invalidation from the ordering fence. Lets the kernel batch invalidations across many addresses and emit a single ordering fence at the end. arch/riscv flush_tlb_* paths use it when available.

mandatory.name: Svnapot
mandatory.description: Naturally-Aligned-Power-of-Two PTE encoding for 64-KiB contiguous mappings
mandatory.layer_note: PTE-format extension: a single PTE can describe a 64-KiB naturally-aligned contiguous mapping (saves TLB pressure without changing the page table tree). Kernel hugetlb (CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_SVNAPOT) and transparent contiguous pages use it. Userspace sees it via mmap(MAP_HUGETLB).

mandatory.name: Svpbmt
mandatory.description: PBMT field in PTE selects memory attributes (PMA, NC, IO)
mandatory.layer_note: PTE bits 62-61 select PMA (default), NC (non-cacheable), or IO (I/O ordering). Kernel: ioremap, pgprot_noncached, pgprot_writecombine, DMA mappings drive PBMT directly instead of region-based PMA. Removes the need for vendor-specific memtype hacks.

mandatory.name: Sv39
mandatory.description: 39-bit virtual addressing with a 3-level page table
mandatory.layer_note: The mandatory minimum address-space size for RVA23S64. Sv48 / Sv57 are optional. Kernel page table walker, VM layout, KASLR, and direct map are all sized around Sv39 as a baseline.

mandatory.name: Zifencei
mandatory.description: FENCE.I instruction for synchronizing instruction fetches with writes to instruction memory
mandatory.layer_note: Kernel uses for module loading, kprobes, eBPF JIT, ftrace. FENCE.I only synchronizes the issuing hart so kernel multi-hart icache flushes also use SBI / IPI. Userspace JIT (V8, JVM) should use the __riscv_flush_icache vDSO / syscall rather than FENCE.I directly.

mandatory.name: Svade
mandatory.description: Hardware updates PTE Accessed and Dirty bits transparently
mandatory.layer_note: Profile property: hardware must update PTE.A on read/exec, PTE.D on write. Kernel can drop the software A/D update fallback. Svadu (optional) is the inverse - hardware that can be told to NOT update A/D.

mandatory.name: Svbare
mandatory.description: satp.MODE = Bare (no translation) must be supported
mandatory.layer_note: Profile property: S-mode must be able to run with no virtual-memory translation (Bare). Software-transparent guarantee that early boot and identity-mapped paths work before MMU enable.

optional.name: Sv48
optional.description: 48-bit virtual addressing with a 4-level page table
optional.layer_note: Larger virtual address space. Kernel selects at boot via DT/ACPI (PAGE_TABLE_LEVELS=4) and starts in Sv48 when available, falling back to Sv39 otherwise.

optional.name: Sv57
optional.description: 57-bit virtual addressing with a 5-level page table
optional.layer_note: Even larger virtual address space (mirrors x86-64 LA57). Kernel runtime-detects via satp probe and starts in Sv57 when supported.

optional.name: Svadu
optional.description: Lets software opt out of hardware A/D bit update via menvcfg.ADUE
optional.layer_note: Inverse of Svade: if implemented, software can write menvcfg.ADUE=0 to suppress hardware A/D update and handle it in the fault path. Rarely useful (real-time / QoS configurations).

optional.name: Svvptc
optional.description: Implementation may cache PTEs by virtual address without the usual SFENCE.VMA requirements
optional.layer_note: Microarchitectural optimization. Software-transparent: kernel can drop a few redundant SFENCE.VMA calls in the transient case, but is not required to.

optional.name: Sdtrig
optional.description: Hardware triggers for breakpoints, watchpoints, and ICOUNT
optional.layer_note: Debug infrastructure: hardware breakpoints/watchpoints/ICOUNT exposed through the Debug Module. Consumed by external debuggers (gdb via OpenOCD) and self-hosted kgdb; not part of Linux's normal ABI.

optional.name: Sspm
optional.description: Pointer masking available *to* S-mode (the kernel itself)
optional.layer_note: Parallel to Supm (U-mode) - announces that the kernel itself can use pointer masking. Few in-kernel consumers exist yet; potential KASAN-style tagged allocator integration.

optional.name: Ssstrict
optional.description: Implementation strictly raises illegal-instruction on any unratified or unallocated opcode
optional.layer_note: Software-transparent profile property guaranteeing the implementation does not silently execute custom or unratified opcodes. Useful for compliance / sandboxing claims.

optional.name: Zkr
optional.description: 'seed' CSR providing access to a hardware entropy source
optional.layer_note: Hardware entropy via CSR read of 'seed'. Kernel RNG (random.c) can seed from it; getrandom() / /dev/urandom paths benefit. Userspace can also read directly when permitted (controlled via mseccfg / sstateen).

summary.scope: S-mode/H-mode additions on top of RVA23U64

by_layer.compiler: Compiler auto-generates - march enables, no other changes
by_layer.kernel: Kernel adaptation needed - userspace largely transparent
by_layer.full_stack: Kernel + compiler + userspace libraries all need work
